meanings.note: Feminine: actrice. Derived with the Romance agent/quality suffix '-eur'/'-euse' (from Latin '-or'/'-tor'). Standard masculine noun meaning 'actor'.
une agence artistique = a talent agency

examples.text: Cette agence ne représente que des stars.

meanings.note: Aider quelqu'un, no preposition. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to help'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'aidé').
Parler anglais = to speak English. Masculine noun ('le anglais', plural 'les anglais') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'English language'.
Un Anglais / une Anglaise. Masculine noun ('le anglais', plural 'les anglais') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'English language'.

examples.text: Elle parle parfaitement anglais avec l'accent.
examples.trans: She speaks English perfectly with the accent.

meanings.note: Une autre = another (one). Descriptive French adjective meaning 'other'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.
Also a pronoun. Descriptive French adjective meaning 'other'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Il y a une autre Clémentine?
L'un à midi, l'autre à deux heures.
examples.trans: One at noon, the other at two.

examples.text: L'un à midi, l'autre à quatorze heures. Je vais déjeuner deux fois.
examples.trans: One at noon, the other at two. I'm going to have lunch twice.

meanings.note: Core French preposition meaning 'with', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.

examples.text: Et demain, tu déjeunes avec Audiard.
examples.trans: And tomorrow you're having lunch with Audiard.

meanings.note: avoir peur = to be afraid, avoir raison = to be right, avoir 40 ans = to be 40

meanings.en: helper verb of the passé composé
meanings.note: J'ai appelé = I called. French '-ir' verb (from Latin '-ire'). Core French verb meaning 'to have'.

meanings.en: il y a = there is, there are
meanings.note: Fixed expression. French '-ir' verb (from Latin '-ire'). Core French verb meaning 'to have'.
beaucoup de + noun, with no article: beaucoup de travail

meanings.en: beaucoup de = a lot of, many
meanings.note: Invariable French adverb meaning 'a lot'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.

examples.trans: You know a lot of people.

examples.text: Tu connais beaucoup de monde dans le cinéma. Tu pourrais m'aider.
examples.trans: You know lots of people in film. You could help me.

meanings.note: Third-group irregular verb inherited from core Latin roots ('-ere'). Core French verb meaning 'to drink'.

examples.trans: Would you like something to drink?

meanings.note: as an interjection: bon, alors... = right, so...
as an interjection: bon, alors... = right, so...

meanings.en: bonne journée = have a nice day
meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'good'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.
Faire un cauchemar. Masculine noun ('le cauchemar', plural 'les cauchemars') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'nightmare'.

examples.text: Je ne dors plus et je fais des cauchemars.
examples.trans: I no longer sleep and I have nightmares.

examples.text: Toute cette histoire ressemble à un cauchemar.
examples.trans: This whole affair resembles a nightmare.

meanings.note: Une paire de chaussures. Feminine noun ('la chaussure', plural 'les chaussures') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'shoe'.

examples.text: J'ai complètement oublié de prendre des chaussures.
examples.trans: I completely forgot to get shoes.

examples.text: Et c'est quoi ces drôles de chaussures?
examples.trans: And what are these funny shoes?

meanings.note: signer un contrat = to sign a contract

examples.text: Je ne connais rien aux contrats.
examples.trans: I don't know anything about contracts.

meanings.note: un cours d'équitation = a riding lesson
Masculine noun ('le cours', plural 'les cours') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'class'.

examples.text: Je suis à mon cours d'équitation.
Gabriel! Je suis à mon cours d'équitation.
examples.trans: Gabriel! I'm at my horse-riding lesson.

meanings.note: D' before a vowel. Core French preposition meaning 'of', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.
le film de Tarantino = Tarantino's film
Also 'some': du sucre. Core French preposition meaning 'of', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.

meanings.en: for (a length of time, still going on)
meanings.note: with the present: je suis là depuis trois mois
Depuis lundi. Core French preposition meaning 'since', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.

examples.text: Je suis seule depuis trois mois.
examples.trans: I've been on my own for three months.

examples.text: Elle n'a pas travaillé depuis deux ans.
examples.trans: She hasn't worked for two years.

meanings.note: The x sounds like z before a vowel. Spoken French num expression meaning 'two', common in natural conversation.

examples.text: Deux places pour mardi? Mardi, tu as le film de Kechiche.
examples.trans: Two tickets for Tuesday? On Tuesday you've got the Kechiche film.

meanings.note: + infinitive. French '-ir' verb (from Latin '-ire'). Core French verb meaning 'must, to have to'.
French '-ir' verb (from Latin '-ire'). Core French verb meaning 'must, to have to'.

examples.trans: I have to see the play.

examples.text: Magali, je dois voir la pièce de Koltès cette semaine.
examples.trans: Magali, I have to see the Koltès play this week.

diriger.gloss: to direct, to manage, to run

meanings.en: to direct (a film, play, orchestra); to run, to manage
meanings.note: keeps 'e' before a/o (nous dirigeons)

examples.text: Il veut écrire, diriger, choisir ses partenaires.
examples.trans: He wants to write, direct, choose his partners.

examples.text: Il veut écrire, diriger, choisir ses partenaires. C'est l'enfer!

meanings.note: en retard = late, en vacances = on holiday

examples.text: Oh non! Je suis en retard.

enchaîner.gloss: to follow on, to chain together

meanings.en: to follow on immediately, to chain together
meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to follow on immediately'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'enchaîné').

examples.text: Je ne peux pas enchaîner deux tournages.
examples.trans: I cannot do two film shoots back-to-back.

examples.text: Je peux pas enchaîner comme ça.
examples.trans: I cannot follow on like that.

examples.text: Et il doit enchaîner avec l'autre film!
examples.trans: And he has to jump straight into the next film!

meanings.note: The t is never pronounced. French conjunction meaning 'and', used to link clauses in spoken and written discourse.

examples.text: Et demain, tu déjeunes avec Audiard.
examples.trans: And tomorrow you're having lunch with Audiard.

meanings.note: fabriquer un trophée = to make a trophy

examples.text: Ils fabriquent la célèbre Palme d'or.
examples.trans: They manufacture the famous Palme d'Or.

meanings.note: Third-group irregular verb inherited from core Latin roots ('-ere'). Core French verb meaning 'to do, to make'.

examples.text: Ça fait une heure que j'attends.
examples.trans: I've been waiting for an hour.

examples.text: C'est le prochain film de Tarantino.
Tu as le film de Kechiche.

Manner adverb formed by adding '-ment' (from Latin 'mente', 'with a ... mind') to the feminine adjective stem.

examples.trans: But finally, we found Samuel's whiskey, so we're not killing ourselves.

meanings.note: C'est fini = it's over. Descriptive French adjective meaning 'finished'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Tu es pourrie! Mais c'est fini.

meanings.note: regular -ir verb (-issons in plural)

meanings.en: finir par + infinitive = to end up doing
meanings.note: French '-ir' verb (from Latin '-ire'). Core French verb meaning 'to finish, to end up'.

examples.text: Je finis par passer pour un idiot!
examples.trans: I end up looking like an idiot!

examples.text: Je finis par passer pour un idiot! Tu sais ce qu'elle a fait?
examples.trans: I end up looking like an idiot! Do you know what she did?

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la forêt', plural 'les forêts') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'forest'.

examples.text: Il y a aussi de grandes forêts!
examples.trans: There are big forests there too!

examples.text: Vous connaissez Rambouillet? Il y a aussi de grandes forêts!
examples.trans: Do you know Rambouillet? There are big forests there too!

meanings.note: colloquial; singular and plural have the same form

examples.text: Le gars du site de rencontres?
examples.trans: The guy from the dating site?

meanings.note: for masculine nouns, and in impersonal phrases: il y a
Also in fixed phrases: il y a. High-frequency French pronoun meaning 'he'; clitic object forms precede the conjugated verb.
Never changes for plural. Spoken French phrase expression meaning 'there is', common in natural conversation.
il y a trois semaines = three weeks ago

examples.text: Il y a une autre Clémentine?
Non, c'est la place de Samuel. Il est mort il y a six jours.
examples.trans: No, it's Samuel's place. He died six days ago.

se laver les mains = to wash one's hands

examples.text: C'est le prochain film de Tarantino.

meanings.note: Mais oui! = of course!. French conjunction meaning 'but', used to link clauses in spoken and written discourse.
Same form in the plural. Masculine noun ('le mois', plural 'les mois') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'month'.

examples.text: Oui, allô? Ça fait des mois que j'attends ton appel!
examples.trans: Yes, hello? I've been waiting for your call for months!

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la méthode', plural 'les méthodes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'acting technique or method'.

examples.text: C'est la méthode de l'Actor Studio.
examples.trans: It is the Actor Studio method.

meanings.note: ne... pas = not; ne... rien = nothing; ne... que = only; n' before a vowel

meanings.note: at the end of a sentence: super, non?
Tag at the end of a question. Invariable French adverb meaning 'no'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.

examples.text: Oh non! Je suis en retard.

examples.text: Tarantino ne prendra pas Cécile. Problème d'âge.

meanings.note: Plein de = full of. Descriptive French adjective meaning 'full'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Écoute, c'est une industrie, et elle est pleine de requins.
examples.trans: Listen, it's an industry, and it's full of sharks.

meanings.note: With ne: je n'en peux plus. Invariable French adverb meaning 'no more'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.
pronounced plys at the end of a sentence in this sense

examples.trans: I can't take any more, Andréa.

+ infinitive: pour voir. Core French preposition meaning 'for', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.

meanings.note: + infinitive. French '-ir' verb (from Latin '-ire'). Core French verb meaning 'can, to be able to'.
conditional: tu pourrais, vous pourriez

Always with an object. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to leave'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'quitté').

examples.text: Magali, je dois voir la pièce de Koltès cette semaine.

meanings.note: Passé composé with 'être'. French '-ir' verb (from Latin '-ire'). Core French verb meaning 'to go out; to leave'.

meanings.note: au studio radio = at the radio studio
